architecture_decisions: - Canonical Project and Engineering Run identities are opaque UUID identities supplied by protected runtime integration; they are not filesystem paths. - Filesystem roots are generated only beneath a server-configured protected allocator root. - Accepted source versions are represented by immutable content-addressed snapshots, not by the continued existence of a mutable working directory. - Repository or starter initialization is mediated only by an injected trusted `SourceProvider` seam that receives canonical protected identity and returns bounded source bytes plus bounded provenance metadata. It does not accept caller URLs, commands, credentials, generic HTTP requests, or arbitrary bootstrap scripts. - This workstream adds no shared database fields and does not edit #59 persistence/schema ownership.
work_items: - Implement a new immutable lineage storage system that validates canonical identity, normalizes and bounds source paths, stores content-addressed blobs, records immutable manifests, tracks one protected current lineage per Project/run pair, detects stale lineage, and reconstructs exact source content. The lineage store validates canonical identity, normalizes and bounds source paths, stores content-addressed blobs, records immutable manifests, tracks one protected current lineage per Project/run pair, detects stale lineage, and reconstructs exact source content.
validations: - The lineage store validates canonical identity, normalizes and bounds source paths, stores content-addressed blobs, records immutable manifests, tracks one protected current lineage per Project/run pair, detects stale lineage, and reconstructs exact source content.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — The lineage boundary accepts only canonical UUID Project and Engineering Run identifiers. `project:<id>`, paths, URLs, blank values and malformed UUIDs are rejected, and filesystem storage locations are derived server-side rather than from raw Project/run text.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — All live source workspaces are created beneath one server-configured allocator root using server-generated lease identities. The initialization, resolve/reconstruct and implementation-acceptance interfaces expose no caller-controlled filesystem-root parameter, and forged/out-of-root workspace leases fail closed.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Initialization and each accepted implementation mutation produce immutable lineage evidence derived from the exact sorted source tree, canonical Project/run identity, parent lineage and bounded provenance. Equivalent accepted inputs are deterministic, while a different tree or different identity produces a different content/lineage identity and cannot be mislabeled as the accepted lineage.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Repository/template/starter initialization occurs only through an injected trusted source provider that receives canonical Project/run identity. The public lineage contract accepts no raw repository URL, generic HTTP request, provider credential, shell command, Git command or arbitrary bootstrap command; provider source paths/content are normalized and bounded before persistence.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — A new implementation lineage may advance only from the current expected parent and must contain an actual source change. Repeating an already-recorded identical implementation result with the same expected parent returns the accepted child lineage idempotently, while a different tree, wrong parent, wrong Project/run identity or stale lineage is rejected without changing the protected current pointer.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Any accepted lineage can be resolved after later mutations and reconstructed into a fresh isolated workspace whose rescanned content digest exactly matches the recorded snapshot. Manifest tampering, blob tampering, missing blobs, identity mismatch or attempts to substitute different content fail integrity validation.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Deleting or expiring a materialized live workspace removes only that server-owned lease. Immutable manifests, content-addressed blobs and protected current-lineage evidence remain available so BUILD/TEST/VERIFY, retry or resume can reconstruct and prove the accepted source version after cleanup.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Source capture enforces explicit maximum file count, per-file bytes and aggregate bytes. Lineage evidence contains bounded canonical identifiers, lineage/content digests, file counts/sizes, source kind and a digest of bounded provenance; it does not expose raw source contents, provider credentials, repository state, secret files or unbounded metadata.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — The new modules expose no user/model-supplied shell, arbitrary HTTP/network, Git history mutation, dependency installation, provider secret handling, Work Specification self-approval, protected-stage success override, Vercel promotion or production deployment operation.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — The worker candidate remains additive to `code/`, tests and `P2-V0.15.2` artifacts, does not edit #59 shared schema/persistence or #61 orchestration paths, and provides a protected source-lineage interface that serialized integration can bind to #59 canonical `project_id`/run identity and #61 IMPLEMENT→BUILD→TEST→VERIFY orchestration without reinterpreting `workspace_ref` as a path.
risks: - No material risk and no mitigation is necessary.
